analysis:
Reviewed the changelog, the docs row (docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 372), the production patch in SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift and the test-only changes in SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (new tests around head lines 3140-3239). The only production change is the header-verdict memo in SSDWholeRootMaintainer: readableHeaderIdentities is a per-root map from file path to lstat identity (dev, ino, size, mtime and ctime with nanoseconds).

T-041 and TB-007 analysis:
- The memo only skips re-parsing a DBK3 header (metadataReadable). That flag gates ownership for TTL, budget and temp cleanup. It does not feed decryption, AES-GCM/AAD verification, lookup-tag derivation or cache-hit logic, so at-rest confidentiality and integrity are unchanged.
- A cached verdict is reused only when the lstat identity is identical and fanoutPassesReadChecks passes once per fanout. That function repeats isSafeModelRoot, pathResolvesToItself, isRealDirectory and the no-follow openDirectoryChain walk, so symlink and unsafe-directory protection is kept.
- ctime and inode are in the identity. Userland cannot set ctime, so a same-UID attacker cannot rewrite the header while preserving the identity. The new tests cover mtime-restored corruption and replacement of a lookalike file.
- Failed reads are never cached, so transient EIO, EMFILE or directory-chain failures cannot hold a block past its TTL. The 30-minute TTL bound is preserved.
- The identity is taken before the read. A concurrent change yields a different identity and a re-read on the next pass.
- The map is rebuilt each pass via defer, so it is bounded to the files currently seen. An early return on a failed guard before the defer leaves the old map untouched, which is harmless.
- ownedContents is invoked under maintenanceLock, which guards the map. The caller was not shown, but the lock comment is consistent with this.

Limits: the post-write trigger for maintenance, and any starvation interaction with writers or the removal lock (T-016, T-060), is not visible in the supplied source. It is not a security conclusion-affecting gap on the evidence. No regression or threat-model invalidation found.
